title: Serve assurance and throttling policy playbook for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: Define a deterministic, auditable SLA and error-budget crediting model for Redwood Dedicated customers that explicitly ties sustained degradation, autoscaler behavior, and temporary throttling to contract credits and customer notifications. This doc captures definitions, measurement windows, credit math, throttling policy when capacity is constrained, and a customer-facing notice template. It also specifies the engineering signals needed to automate credit computation and interlock with the autoscaler to avoid cascading failures.
background: We've historically offered throughput guarantees as a broad entitlement. As Dedicated adoption grows, sales/legal require a more prescriptive, measurable framework that covers: (1) how sustained degradation is detected (metrics & windows), (2) how credits are calculated and applied, (3) when we may proactively throttle to protect global stability and how customers are notified, and (4) how autoscaler triggers interact with SLA measurements.
definitions: Committed Tokens Per Minute (CTPM): The customer-contracted steady-state tokens/min allocated to the dedicated pool.
Measured Supply (MS): The observed tokens/min served by the dedicated pool, computed per-AZ and aggregated across the customer's scope.
Degradation Window: A contiguous time window of N minutes where MS < threshold determined by CTMP percentile (see measurement rules).

Error Budget: Cumulative minutes of degradation allowed in a billing period before credits escalate. Error budget is measured in token-minutes shortfall and converted to monetary credit per contract formula.
Proactive Throttle: An automated, reversible rate limit applied to new requests when autoscaler capacity is saturated and global risk of multi-customer degradation is high.
measurement_rules: Primary metric: tokens_served_per_minute at the customer pool level, sampled and computed per 1-minute bucket.
Latency & p99: p99 request latency is recorded independently; a latency-driven degradation is counted when p99 exceeds contract threshold for the same Degradation Window.

Window sizing: Standard Degradation Window = 15 minutes (configurable per contract). Shorter windows (5 minutes) allowed for burst-focused tiers; longer windows (60 minutes) allowed where volatility is expected.
Aggregation: To compute MS we use median-of-AZs after excluding any AZs flagged by infra health monitors during the window to avoid noisy spikes from AZ-level incidents.
Data sources: telemetry from serving runtime (token counters), console ingestion pipeline (metric-normalization), and the incident event bus for correlated outages.
credit_calculation: Step 1: For each minute in the billing period, compute shortfall = max(0, CTPM - MS).
Step 2: Sum shortfall across the billing window to obtain token-minutes shortfall S.
Step 3: Convert S to monetary credit via: credit = S * unit_credit_rate where unit_credit_rate = contract_unit_price_per_token / expected_token_efficiency_factor.
Example: CTPM=120k, sustained MS=90k for a 30-min Degradation Window -> S = (120k-90k)*30 = 900k token-minutes. If unit_credit_rate = $0.0000005 per token-minute -> credit = $0.45.
Proportional caps: Per-contract max monthly credit = min(configured_cap, credit). Credits are additive across events in a billing period until cap is hit.

Partial mitigation: If automated autoscale remedied a portion of the shortfall within the Degradation Window, apply a 50% mitigation factor to the reduced minutes unless customer provided scaling override.
throttling_policy: Goal: Prefer graceful degradation via prioritized routing & admission control rather than hard global failures. Throttling is a last-resort protective measure when backend capacity is exhausted.

Trigger conditions: Proactive Throttle may be applied when (a) cluster free capacity < 5% for 3 consecutive minutes, (b) global error-rate spike correlated with sustained high queue lengths, and (c) autoscaler cannot add capacity within the configured burst window.

Behavior: Throttling is applied as a per-customer token-burst limit which reduces new allocation but preserves warm KV-caches for in-flight sessions. Throttle levels escalate in 3 steps (mild, moderate, severe) with automated rollback when supply stabilizes.
Customer opt-out: Customers may opt-in to a ‘best-effort’ non-throttled mode in exchange for reduced SLA guarantees and explicit billing uplift. This must be signed and added to contract addendum.
Transparency: Every throttle event generates a structured notification (console banner + email + webhook) that includes reason, duration, effect on CTPM, and how credits will be assessed.
autoscaler_interlock: Autoscaler signals consumed for SLA measurement: active_gpus, queue_length, average_sequence_length, and p99_latency.

Autoscale policy must expose a read-only event stream that flags scale-up intent timestamps. If scale-up intent was issued but blocked (e.g., capacity quota), that window is excluded from credit calculation after manual validation.

Handover rules: If autoscaler executes scale-up within the Degradation Window and recovers MS by >= 80% of CTPM, degrade minutes are discounted using the Partial mitigation rule in credit_calculation.
Pull vs. push: Implementation requires a push-based event to the billing/credit engine with canonicalized JSON events (see links). Engineering must supply a schema and retention guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: SLA spec reviewed & signed off by Legal and Sales for the standard Dedicated Tiers.
Telemetry pipelines emit tokens_served_per_minute and autoscaler intent events to the billing engine with < 60s lag in 90th percentile.
Console shows a 'Dedicated Serve Health' panel with CTPM vs MS over rolling 7d and a computed running error budget for customer view.
Notification templates are approved and implemented for console banners, email, and webhook payloads.
Credit computation is validated end-to-end on the staging billing pipeline with 3 synthetic degradation scenarios and signed test reports.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): Apply to two pilot customers on dedicated-small pools for 6 weeks. Monitor false positives and credit accuracy.
Phase 2 (opt-in): Offer as opt-in contract addendum to new customers and existing customers willing to accept the standard thresholds.
Phase 3 (default): Make standard for all new Dedicated contracts after legal approval and telemetry SLO attainment.
Rollback: If credit miscomputations exceed 0.1% of billed amount in pilot, pause rollout and run forensic on metric pipeline.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metric skew from noisy AZs causes false degrading events. Mitigation: Use median-of-AZs and exclude flagged AZs per measurement rules.
Risk: Autoscaler event lag causes disputed credits. Mitigation: Store event-level evidence with checksums and expose a dispute workflow for customers.
Risk: Throttling surprises customers. Mitigation: Clear opt-in/opt-out documentation, pre-event console banners for predicted throttles, and a 30-minute pre-notice for scheduled capacity maintenance.
Regulatory: Billing adjustments must be auditable. Mitigation: All computed credits and inputs retained for 13 months and exportable via request.
